faq.q: How does a coil of wire become a magnet?
faq.a: Every current makes a magnetic field around its wire. Wind the wire into a coil and the fields of all the loops add together into one strong field, like a bar magnet's.

faq.q: Why does an electromagnet have an iron core?
faq.a: Iron is made of tiny magnetic regions that line up with the coil's field, making it hundreds of times stronger. Soft iron also loses its magnetism as soon as the current stops.
asks: What does the iron nail do in an electromagnet?

faq.q: What can an electromagnet pick up?
faq.a: Things made of iron, steel, nickel or cobalt. Big electromagnets on cranes lift scrap cars in a scrapyard and drop them when the current is switched off.

faq.q: How do you make an electromagnet stronger?
faq.a: Use more current, wind more turns of wire, or add an iron core. Each of these makes the magnetic field stronger.
asks: What makes an electromagnet more powerful?

faq.q: What happens when you switch off an electromagnet?
faq.a: With no current there is no field from the coil, and a soft iron core loses its magnetism almost at once, so whatever it was holding drops.

facts: William Sturgeon built the first electromagnet in 1824.
Doubling the current or the number of turns roughly doubles an electromagnet's strength, until the iron core is fully magnetised.

quiz.say: Which change would make an electromagnet weaker?
quiz.show: Which change would make an electromagnet weaker?
quiz.why: Fewer turns means fewer loops adding their fields together, so the magnet is weaker.

wrong.1: An iron core makes it much stronger.
wrong.2: More current makes a stronger field.
